sentences.text: Shri D. Chelawat, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Vivek Dalal, learned AAG on behalf of the respondent/State.
Heard.

The petitioner before this Court has filed the present petition being aggrieved by the order dated 31.01.2020 passed by District Magistrate, District Dhar in exercise of power conferred under M.P. Rajya Suraksha Adhinium, 1990 and also being aggrived by order passed in appeal dated 16.03.2020 passed by Divisional Commissioner, Division Indore.
Facts of the case reveal that based upon two incidents of the year 2013 and 2015 relating to the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the order of externment has been passed.

The other important aspect of the case as reflected from paragraph no.6 of the order passed by District Magistrate is that the offence committed by the petitioner falls under Chapter-16 (Section 272 of IPC) and in those circumstances, the order has been passed.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued before this Court that so far as the incident of 2015 is concerned, appeal is pending and stay has been granted in favour of the present petitioner.
He has filed the documents also to that effect at page no.20.
The order passed by the appellate court reflects that the order passed by the District Magistrate has been stayed.
Meaning thereby, only on the basis of incident of 2013, the order of externment has been passed.

Relevant statutory provisions governing the field as contained under Sections 3, 5 and 6 of M.P.
Rajya Suraksha Adhinium, 1990 reads as under...
3. Power to make restriction order. - (1) If a District Magistrate is satisfied with respect to any persons that he is acting or is likely to act in a manner prejudicial to the security of the State or the maintenance of public order and that, in order to prevent him from so acting it is necessary in the interest of the general public to make an order under this Section, the District Magistrate, may make an order,-
(a) requiring him to notify movements or to report himself or both to notify his movements and report himself in such manner at such times and to such authority or Mukesh Bafna vs State Of M.P. Through Health Department on 14 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51589884/
1 persons as may be specified in the order;
(b) imposing upon him such restrictions as may be specified in the order, in respect of his association or communications with such persons as may be mentioned in the order;
(c) prohibiting or restricting the possession or use by him of any such article or articles as may be specified in the order.
(2) A restriction order made under sub-section (1) shall remain in operation for such period as may be specified therein and shall in no case exceed a period of one year from the date of the order.
5. Removal of persons about to commit offence. - Whenever it appears to the District Magistrate- (a) that the movements or acts of any person are causing or calculated to cause alarm,
danger or harm to person or property; or (b) that there are reasonably grounds for believing that such person is engaged or is about to be engaged in the commission of an offence involving force or violence or an offence punishable under Chapter XII, XVI or XVII or under Section 506 or 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860) or in the abatement of any such offence,
and when in the opinion of the District Magistrate witnesses are not willing to come forward to give evidence in public against such person by reason of apprehension on their part as regards the safety of their person or property; or (c) that an outbreak of epidemic disease is likely to result from the continued residence of an immigrant;
the District Magistrate may, by an order in writing duty served on him or by beat of drum or otherwise as the District Magistrate thinks fit, direct such person or immigrant- (a) so as to conduct himself as shall seem necessary in order to prevent violence and alarm or the outbreak or spread of such disease; or (b) to remove himself outside the district or my part thereof or such area and any district or districts or any part thereof, contiguous thereto by such route within such time as the District Magistrate may specify and not to enter or return to the said district or part thereof or such area and such contiguous districts, or part thereof, as the case may be, from which he was directed to remove himself.
6. Removal of persons convicted of certain offences.

sentences.text: Shri Dalal, learned AAG on behalf of State has vehemently argued before this Court that action has been initiated against the petitioner as he was involved in adulteration activities.
This Court has carefully gone through the reply and also the record.
Section 5 certainly not at all covers the present case.
There was no material to establish that the movements or acts of the petitioner are going to cause or calculated to cause alarm or danger to any person or property.
Not only this, Section 6 of M.P. Rajya Suraksha Adhinium, 1990 does not include the offences under Chapter-16 (Section 272 of IPC)

and in those circumstances, as he was not convicted for the offence included under Chapter-16, the impugned order deserved to be set aside and is accordingly set aside.
Based upon one or two stray incidents of 2013 and 2015 vintage, the order has been passed under the M.P. Rajya Suraksha Adhinium, 1990.
One of the incident of 2015 is under judicial scrutiny and stay has been granted by the appellate Court and therefore, there appears to be non application of mind on the part of the authorities.
Resultantly, the petition is allowed and the impugned orders passed by the District Magistrate and the appellate authority are hereby quashed.
Cc as per rules.
